name: Session-ending orders
description: The transactional outbox of every "end this session" order (docs/audits/2026-11-03-redis-outage.md): a device kick for the MQTT gateway's iot:kicks stream, a websocket control order for the realtime gateway's ws:control:stream. An order is written in the same database transaction as the change that causes it (a device deleted, a credential revoked, a session revoked, a member removed, a tenant suspended), delivered right after the commit, and otherwise relayed every 5 s, oldest first, until Redis takes it; each carries a stable id so a reader acts on it once. A pending order older than a minute raises an alert and a metric; one the relay gives up on is kept as a dead letter for an operator. The hosts that end a person's access (user_session, tenant_member, tenant) record the orders of modules they cannot depend on (websocket_session's socket drops) through its point session_end:order_source, inside their own transaction (D249). A library and a relay: no UI, no tenant-facing route.
author: Kuray Karaaslan

extensionPoints.description: The session-ending orders a change that ends access must carry in its own transaction (D249): the host (user_session revoking sessions, tenant_member ending or changing a membership, tenant suspending, deleting or purging a tenant) calls recordSessionEndInTx(qr, cause) before its commit, and each contribution answers the orders the cause needs (ordersFor(cause) => SessionEndOrderInput[]; pure: no database, no Redis, never the host's transaction; every order names the cause's tenant). session_end records them in the host's transaction and delivers them after the commit. A contribution that fails or answers something invalid never blocks the change: it is logged, counted and left to its after-commit hook. Gate data, as the hosts' own hooks.

extensions.description: The session-ending outbox, platform-wide, listed for the ROOT tenant only: an order older than a minute not yet in Redis (MAJOR, opens an incident) and dead-lettered orders (CRITICAL). One alert per condition, never per tenant.
